title: Life in Galia
description: Meet the factions, political tensions, and species identity that give Star Atlas its universe-level character.
heroTitle: A premium sci-fi universe needs factions with real texture.
heroSummary: This page distills the political and cultural shape of Galia into a smaller number of stronger ideas so the universe feels memorable instead of encyclopedic.
utilityLine: The redesign uses progressive disclosure here: enough worldbuilding to build trust, without forcing lore homework.

heroMedia.label: Faction preview
heroMedia.caption: Faction identity is now presented as a product advantage, not just a lore archive.

heroPanel.title: Faction texture makes every other page feel more alive.
heroPanel.body: Game loops, economy decisions, and community identity all become more compelling when the universe gives them meaningful contrast.
bullets: A stronger reason to pick a side

sections.heading: Three power centers. Three different futures.

cards.title: Industrial confidence
cards.body: MUD channels human expansion through production capacity, pragmatic ambition, and a recognizably physical presence.

cards.title: Coalition intelligence
cards.body: ONI represents plurality, adaptation, and the strategic advantage of shared expertise across species.

cards.title: Precision and optimization
cards.body: Ustur creates the cold, elegant counterpoint that every premium sci-fi setting needs.

sections.heading: Lore is strongest when it sharpens player choice.
body: The redesign trims exposition and keeps the emphasis on decision-making. Faction identity matters because it changes how the universe feels, not because the site dumps every detail up front.
That makes the page easier to absorb while still preserving the sense of a larger world beyond the marketing shell.
sections.asideTitle: The universe page should create attraction, not homework.
sections.asideBody: It exists to deepen desire and confidence, not to force encyclopedic reading before action.

sections.heading: Short answers that keep the page moving.

items.question: Why avoid deep lore walls here?
items.answer: Because this page is a gateway. The job is to create clarity and desire, then let the universe expand through later pages and community channels.

items.question: What should someone do after this page?
items.answer: Either move into Galia for the frontier context or into the newsroom and roadmap for a clearer picture of how the world is evolving.

finalCta.title: Carry the universe into play and progress.
finalCta.text: See the frontier, follow the roadmap, or move into gameplay systems that turn faction identity into stakes.
